chunks.content: ## Overview of T-Shirt Loewenling Ribbed Collar Construction This section explains the process of creating the ribbed collar for a T-shirt using CLO software, focusing on placement, sewing, folding, simulation, and fabric application. Key terms include arrangement points, sewing lines, fold lines, adjustment panels, and fabric pattern application. --- ## Positioning the Loewenling (Ribbed Collar) on the T-Shirt Start by placing the T-shirt in the workspace. Open the arrangement points and position the Loewenling (the ribbed collar piece) at an appropriate arrangement point. Since the ribbed collar ends on the back side, place it opposite the T-shirt’s arrangement point. Adjust the position by setting the distance between the arrow and the X marker to ensure precise alignment before sewing. --- ## Sewing the Ribbed Collar Use the Free Sewing tool (1 to N) for stitching: 1. Sew "Rowan 1" (likely referring to the first sewing segment). 2. Hold the Shift key and sew the circular edge of the ribbed collar. 3. Begin sewing from the back side. 4. Sew along both sides of the "Rowan" (the collar piece). This sequence ensures the ribbed collar is securely attached. --- ## Simulation and Adjustment After Sewing After sewing: - Run the simulation by pressing the Control key. - Switch to the Adjustment panel tool. - Right-click on the panel and select "Print" (likely to finalize or inspect the sewing line layout). - Run the simulation again. - Turn off the simulation to proceed with manual adjustments. --- ## Creating and Managing Fold Lines To shape the ribbed collar properly: 1. Use the tool to select the top and bottom edges. 2. Create a fold line exactly in the middle between these edges. 3. Display the inner line for clarity. 4. Use the Fold Arrangement tool to select the inner fold line. 5. Employ the positioning ball and the tool tip to execute the fold. 6. While folding, rotate the model to verify if flipping is necessary, ensuring the grid does not fold incorrectly. 7. Set the fold angle to zero for a flat fold. 8. Sew the top and bottom lines with the sewing line type set to "Turn" — this step is crucial for correct folding behavior. --- ## Final Simulation and Panel Adjustments After fold line creation and sewing: - Simulate the garment again. - Use the panel tool to select and untie the panel (likely detaching it to allow further manipulation). - Simulate again to verify changes. --- ## Applying Fabric Patterns To apply the fabric design: - Locate the fabric pattern in the library window. - Select the panel (ribbed collar). - Apply the fabric pattern to the panel. - Confirm application. Simulate once more to observe the fabric on the garment, then stop the simulation. --- ## Refining Fold Lines and Quality Control Inspect the fold line on the ribbed collar's pattern circle: - If the fold line appears uneven, use the Inner Line tool to add 1 mm increment to the fold line.

chunks.content: --- ## Applying Fabric Patterns To apply the fabric design: - Locate the fabric pattern in the library window. - Select the panel (ribbed collar). - Apply the fabric pattern to the panel. - Confirm application. Simulate once more to observe the fabric on the garment, then stop the simulation. --- ## Refining Fold Lines and Quality Control Inspect the fold line on the ribbed collar's pattern circle: - If the fold line appears uneven, use the Inner Line tool to add 1 mm increment to the fold line. - Add grid detail to make the fold line smoother and more rounded. This refinement ensures better garment quality and accurate folding. --- ## Sewing Needle Placement and Final Settings Follow the rule that the sewing needle must hit each bend of the pattern precisely. Adjust the following parameters accordingly: - Volt (fold or dart measurement) - Width - Divide - Set a specified value to 0 (likely a parameter controlling stitch or fold behavior) These settings help ensure consistent stitch quality and pattern accuracy. --- ## Summary This tutorial covers the detailed steps to create a ribbed collar (Loewenling) on a T-shirt using CLO software, including precise placement, sewing, fold line creation, fabric application, simulation, and fine adjustments. Critical steps involve managing arrangement points, using the Free Sewing tool, fold arrangement with zero-angle folds, and fabric pattern application to enhance garment realism and quality.
